UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                   BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                          )        Docket No. ER26-3380-000

                                      COMMENTS OF
                              AMERICAN MUNICIPAL POWER, INC.

         American Municipal Power, Inc. (“AMP”) hereby provides its comments on the July

31, 2026 filing by PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) in the above-captioned docket,1 in

which PJM proposed revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) and

Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load Serving Entities (“RAA”) to establish a

Reliability Backstop Procurement (“RBP”) for the PJM region.

         The RBP is “a one-time time procurement of new capacity to address resource

adequacy challenges in the PJM Region.”2 The mechanism is designed to procure a

targeted quantity of capacity under fixed agreements with terms up to fifteen years

beginning with the 2028/2029 Delivery Year and ending with the 2042/2043 Delivery

Year.3 PJM has set this Initial RBP Target at 6,831.3 MW,4 which may be decremented

to account for certain new offsetting capacity (Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW), as well

as for any qualifying Electric Distributor zone/areas that opt out of procuring capacity

through the RBP. While the RBP will procure capacity on an RTO-wide basis, the capacity

target (and associated costs) will be allocated to specific Electric Distributor zone/areas



1   PJM, Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address Resource Adequacy Concerns Stemming from Large
    Loads, Docket No. ER26-3380-000 (July 31, 2026) (“PJM Filing”).
2   PJM Filing, Transmittal Letter at 1.
3   Id. at 8.
4   This quantity (in megawatts (“MW”) of Unforced Capacity (“UCAP”)) is the amount that PJM’s Base
    Residual Auction for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year cleared short of PJM’s RTO-wide reliability
    requirement at the price cap of $325/MW-day. Id. at 7.
 in PJM, with a further allocation of costs to Load Serving Entities (“LSEs”) located in the

zone/areas that receive an allocation.

         PJM has effectively confirmed that neither AMP, nor any AMP member, will be

allocated any of the costs of procuring the Initial RBP Target (i.e., RBP Charges) under

PJM’s proposal, as all AMP members appear to be within zone/areas that do not receive

any allocation of the Initial RBP Target. AMP strongly supports PJM’s proposal in this

respect, as any allocation of RBP Charges to AMP or its members would be inconsistent

with cost causation principles and the Ratepayer Protection Pledge. Because the PJM

Filing is potentially ambiguous regarding allocation of the Initial RBP Target among the

zone/areas, however, AMP submits these comments to clarify and complete the record.

Additionally, PJM’s Filing demonstrates an administrative error with regard to the

zone/area definition that PJM should address.

I.       COMMENTS

         A.       PJM appropriately allocates the Initial RBP Target to zone/areas with
                  large load growth documented in forecast load adjustments.

         The critical first step in assigning cost responsibility for RBP Charges is PJM’s

allocation of the Initial RBP Target, which PJM appropriately proposes to assign “to each

Electric Distributor’s zone/area using that zone/area’s pro-rata share of the difference

between the forecasted Load Adjustments for the 2026/2027 Delivery Year and the

2028/2029 Delivery Year.”5 In other words, the Initial RBP Target of 6,831.3 MW will be




5    PJM Filing, Attach. A, proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(a).



                                                     2
 allocated to those Electric Distributor zone/areas that have provided to PJM projections

of large load growth between 2026 and 2028.6

         Although there are several more steps in determining ultimate liability for RBP

Charges, zone/areas that do not receive any allocation at this first step are effectively

excluded from responsibility for RBP Charges. As PJM explains, this allocation framework

is consistent with cost causation principles and the Ratepayer Protection Pledge.7

         B.      PJM should clarify the definition of “zone/area” is the one accepted by
                 the Commission in Docket No. ER26-2447.

         While AMP supports PJM’s proposal to allocate the Initial RBP Target to

zone/areas with large load growth, there appears to be a ministerial issue with the

definition of “zone/area” in the PJM Filing. Specifically, the filing includes a definition of

zone/area that does not reflect revisions accepted by the Commission in Docket No.

ER24-2447.8 In that proceeding, PJM proposed to amend the RAA to add the new defined

term “Large Load Adjustment,” which, in turn, included a definition of zone/area.9 In



6   See, e.g., id., Attach. C, Croop Aff. at ¶¶ 41-43; Transmittal Letter at 96-97 (“PJM is proposing to allocate
    daily RBP Charges to relevant Electric Distributor zones/areas, pro rata, based on the zone/area’s
    assigned share of the total, region-wide Final RBP Target MW, floored at zero, and in accordance with
    RAA Schedule 8, as revised in 2024 to incorporate Load Adjustments in equations that ‘specify that load
    forecasts will be adjusted by zone/area and specifically include a variable for Load Adjustments[.]’”); see
    id. at 101.
7   See id., Transmittal Letter at 100-108.
8   See PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 188 FERC ¶ 61,200 (2024), compliance filing accepted, Letter Order,
    Docket Nos. ER24-2447-002, -003 (May 1, 2025).
9   PJM originally proposed the following definition for Large Load Adjustment:
         "Large Load Adjustment" shall mean any MW quantity of adjustments to summer peak load
         at the "zone/area" level and summed by Zone as further detailed in PJM Manuals. For
         purposes of this definition, a "zone/area" is an area within a Zone for which the relevant
         Electric Distributor specifies a separate Obligation Peak Load MW value. A zone/area is a
         service area of an Electric Distributor that is a separately identifiable, geographic area
         bounded by wholesale metering (e.g., the service territory of an operating company of a
         Transmission Owner).
    PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 188 FERC ¶ 61,200 at P 6 (quoting PJM, Intra-PJM Tariffs, RAA Article 1
    -- Definitions (48.0.0)).



                                                       3
 response to concerns raised by AMP that PJM’s proposed definition of zone/area was

potentially ambiguous, the Commission required PJM to revise the definition.10 The

Commission also directed PJM to remove the word “Large” from the proposed term

“Large Load Adjustment.”11 PJM made the required compliance filing,12 which the

Commission accepted in an unreported letter order on May 1, 2025.13

          The RAA definitions included in the PJM Filing do not reflect the revised zone/area

definition accepted by the Commission; rather, the Filing reflects the definitions for “Large

Load Adjustment” and “zone/area” included in PJM’s original filing in Docket No. ER24-

2447.14 Although the PJM Filing appears to utilize the currently effective eTariff version

of the RAA definitions,15 the Commission has made clear that the FERC-accepted version

of a tariff is the filed rate, even if not reflected in eTariff.16




10   Id. at P 41.
11 Id. at P 42.

12 PJM’s compliance filing proposed the following revised definition of “Load Adjustment:”

          “Load Adjustment” shall mean any MW quantity of adjustments to summer peak load at
          the “zone/area” level and summed by Zone as further detailed in PJM Manuals. For
          purposes of this definition, a “zone/area” is the service area within a Zone for which the
          relevant Electric Distributor specifies a separate Obligation Peak Load (OPL) MW value
          that is a separately identifiable, geographic area bounded by wholesale metering (e.g., the
          service territory of an operating company of a Transmission Owner).
     PJM, Amendment to Compliance Filing to Clarify Terms Related to Capacity Obligations for Load
     Adjustments, Docket No. ER24-2447-003, at Attach. A (Dec. 23, 2024).
13   PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Letter Order, Docket Nos. ER24-2447-002, -003 (May 1, 2025).
14   See PJM Filing, Attach. A, RAA Article 1 – Definitions.
15   See RAA Article 1 – Definitions (55.0.0),
     https://etariff.ferc.gov/TariffSectionDetails.aspx?tid=1731&sid=373284. The version accepted by the
     Commission in Docket No. ER24-2447-003 (48.2.0) was accepted on May 1, 2025 to be effective
     August 21, 2024, but it was superseded effective March 24, 2025 by RAA revisions submitted in
     Docket No. ER25-1022-000. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Letter Order, Docket Nos. ER25-1022-00
     (March 4, 2025).
16   Lackawanna Energy Ctr. v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 187 FERC ¶ 61,089, at P 54, order on
     reh’g,189 FERC ¶ 61,029, at P 28 (2024).



                                                      4
          The revisions to the definition of zone/area accepted in Docket No. ER24-2447-

003 were for clarification purposes, and do not appear to materially impact the substantive

meaning of the term.17 Given the importance of zone/areas in the RBP Charge allocation

framework, however, PJM should specifically address the discrepancy between the

definition of zone/area in the PJM Filing and the version accepted by the Commission in

Docket No. ER24-2447-003.

         C.      The PJM Filing is potentially ambiguous regarding the Initial RBP
                 Target allocation.

         Because the allocation of the Initial RBP Target determines the Electric Distributor

zone/areas that will be responsible for RBP Charges, clarity is essential regarding which

zone/areas are receiving such an allocation, and those that are not.18 Unfortunately, the

PJM Filing and related communications leave some ambiguity on this important issue.

         The affidavit of Danielle Croop accompanying the PJM Filing states that:

                 the total region-wide Initial RBP Target is allocated to each
                 Electric Distributor zone/area in accordance with Schedule 8
                 of the RAA, which was revised in 2024 to incorporate Load
                 Adjustments by Electric Distributor zone/area. More
                 specifically, the allocation of RBP UCAP MW to specific
                 Electric Distributor zones/areas will be based on the
                 forecasted load growth from the 2026/2027 Delivery Year to
                 the 2028/2029 Delivery Year and incorporate the Load
                 Adjustments set forth in PJM Table B9b from the 2026 PJM




17   The Commission was principally concerned that, as originally proposed by PJM, “the two-sentence
     definition of ‘zone/area’ within the definition of Large Load Adjustment is ambiguous because the two
     sentences could be read together or separately, and it is therefore unclear whether a zone/area must
     meet both conditions.” PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 188 FERC ¶ 61,200 at P 41. PJM addressed this
     concern by making the definition a single sentence. See supra note 12.
18   Cf., Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 182 FERC ¶ 61,100, at P 34 (2023) (explaining that “Section 205 of the FPA
     and the Commission's regulations require that rates be ‘clearly and specifically’ stated. These
     requirements ensure that the public has adequate notice of the proposed rate, and that the Commission
     has an opportunity to evaluate the proposal to ensure that it is just and reasonable and not unduly
     discriminatory or preferential.” (citation modified)).



                                                     5
                  Load Forecast to ultimately determine the initial allocated pro-
                 rata share to each relevant Electric Distributor zone/area.19

RBP Target:20




Further, PJM provided an additional table as part of an August 10, 2026 stakeholder

presentation regarding the RBP process, which appears to confirm the positive

allocations to specific zone-areas and added information regarding certain zone/areas

that will receive a zero obligation:21

     Interconnection,     L.L.C.,   Tab      Table      B9b    (Feb.     2026),    https://www.pjm.com/-

     [https://perma.cc/J24E-7CV7] (describing Table B9b results)).
20   Id. ¶ 46.
21   PJM and Charles River Assoc., Reliability Backstop Procurement Execution, at 11 (Aug. 10, 2026),
     https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/cifp-rbp/2026/20260810/20260810-pjm-
     and-cra-reliability-backstop-procurement-presentation.pdf.



                                                    6
          These tables account for the entire Initial RBP Target of 6,831.3 MW to be

allocated across fourteen zone/areas, and the latter table notes fifteen other zone/areas

specifically identified as receiving an allocation of zero. PJM has, however, pointed to its

PJM Long-Term Load Forecast EDC/LSE Submission Template as containing the

definitive list of zone/areas within PJM, and there are 160 listed.22 PJM’s specific

identification of the Initial RBP Target allocation of zero for some, but not all, zone/areas

in the table above (aside from those receiving an Initial Share of RBP Charges) creates




22   See PJM Large Load adjustment request template, Zone-Areas tab, https://www.pjm.com/-
     /media/DotCom/committees-groups/subcommittees/las/postings/large-load-adjustment-request-
     template-2027-load-forecast.xlsx (attached hereto as Exhibit A).



                                               7
 potential confusion as to the treatment of zone/areas that should have an allocation of

zero but are not listed.

         Each of AMP’s members in PJM23 operates an electric distribution system for

which the relevant Electric Distributor specifies (or could specify) a separate Obligation

Peak Load, and is located within a separately identifiable, geographic area bounded by

wholesale metering (i.e., each should qualify as a potential zone/area). PJM has

confirmed that only the zone/areas identified as receiving an Initial Share of RBP Charges

in the tables above will face RBP Charges, and that RBP Charges will not be shifted from

one zone/area to another. None of AMP’s members appear to be situated within

zone/areas to which PJM is allocating any portion of the Initial RBP Target, and therefore

none should bear any RBP Charges. Given the potential ambiguity on this issue,

however, these comments are intended to ensure the record is clear regarding the

treatment of AMP and its members for purposes of the Initial RBP Target allocation.




23   Including AMP member Delaware Municipal Electric Corporation’s individual members.



                                                   8
 II.   CONCLUSION

      WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, American Municipal Power, Inc. submits

its comments in this proceeding and asks that the Commission consider them in acting

on the PJM Filing.
